description: Minimal StudySpec contract. Fields under 'consequential' must be set (or explicitly marked as an assumption) before a design is final. system is the setting the experimental units live in; study_type the kind of study; assays the measurements.

field_notes.power.solve_for: set to "reps" when the user asks how many per group: run a power sweep over power.reps_range instead of assuming a replicate count
field_notes.power.reps_range: [min, max] replicate counts for the sweep (rules.tsv layout_default power.reps_range)
field_notes.genetics.unit: what the genetic unit is: line (panel/population of lines or individuals), bulk (BSA, QTL-seq, MutMap pools) or population (selection scans, pool-seq per population)
field_notes.genetics.bulk_fraction: percent tail of the phenotype distribution each bulk takes
field_notes.design.checks: check entries of an augmented design (a count or names)
field_notes.power.solve_for_reason: "asked" (the user asked how many) or "not_stated" (no replicate count given)
field_notes.assay_kinds: finer assay names read from the text (rules.tsv assay_kind), e.g. dnase_seq, faire_seq, amplicon_16s, crispr_screen, proteomics, mpra; assays keeps the coarse labels
field_notes.population.derived_generation: generation the lines were derived from (F2:3 -> 2)
field_notes.repeated_factors: occasion factors (time, stage, age) measured on the same units at every level: [] = different units at each level (destructive), absent = not stated (asked). Listed factors are within-unit in the layout and the unit is a random effect, (1 | unit); also in analysis.terms.repeated_factors
field_notes.factors[].values: numeric level values read from the text ("at 24, 48 and 72 h": [24, 48, 72]); levels then carry the labels ("24 h", ...)
field_notes.factors[].unit: unit of factors[].values: time (rules.tsv time_unit_name: min, h, d, wk, mo, yr) or any other numeric factor (level_unit_name: mg/kg, uM, %, Gy, ...)
field_notes.analysis.goals: analysis goals this study answers, most important first (ids from inst/registry/analysis_goals.json); read from the question, else defaults by data type (rules.tsv goal_default), else treatment_effect; an assumed goal is listed in assumptions["analysis.goals"]
field_notes.analysis.primary_goal: the first goal: Biodes sizes the replicate sweep for it (power.goal, power.reps_range widened by the registry replicate_multiplier), Simitall plants truth for it
field_notes.analysis.goal_terms: per goal id, the generic model terms the goal tests: interaction two terms (time allowed; "env" for several locations/seasons), time_course the time term, trend the numeric term. The model is extended with the interaction/time/numeric term when the catalog model lacks it (noted in analysis.note)
field_notes.analysis.goal_effect: per goal id {size, scale, definition}; scale is the model scale for the data type (rules.tsv effect_scale): identity (continuous outcome), log2 (counts: RNA-seq, peaks, amplicons, intensities), M (methylation), logit (binary, ordinal), log (count outcome), log_hazard (survival); an interaction is a difference of differences on that scale; size = power.minimum_detectable_difference when stated, else listed in assumptions; time_course also {shape: monotone|saturating|transient|delayed, peak {value, unit}, half_time {value, unit}, scope: within_group} when stated; trend size is a change per unit of log10(x + log_offset) or x, set only when the question states one (else assumptions: use the treatment effect over the factor's range); time_course scope within_group adds group (the word, e.g. "infected") and group_factor (the factor it belongs to); trend adds per_unit (the unit the size is per: "kg N/ha", or "log10 uM" for a log-scaled factor); a change stated per a linear amount ("per 50 kg N") makes the factor linear (assumptions["factors.<name>.scale"]); time_course group is a level of group_factor when one matches; survival: scale hazard_ratio (size = target_hazard_ratio), time_ratio (aft) or rmst_difference (with tau)
field_notes.power.goal: the goal the replicate sweep is sized for (= analysis.primary_goal)
field_notes.power.reps_note: why the replicate range was widened, or that stated replicates may be few for the goal
field_notes.factors[].scale: linear, or log when the positive numeric values are equally spaced on a log scale (1, 10, 100; 6, 12, 24, 48)
field_notes.factors[].log_offset: with scale = log and a zero level: fit log10(x + log_offset); log_offset = the smallest positive level
field_notes.factors[].log_base: base of a log-scaled factor (10): fit log10(x + log_offset)
field_notes.factors[].levels: level labels; a two-level pair written "X and Y" carries its names ("wild type", "mutant")
field_notes.primary_outcome.unit: unit the outcome and its effects are stated in (rules.tsv outcome_unit_name: t/ha, cm, mg/dL, %, ...)
field_notes.primary_outcome.baseline_mean: stated usual level of the outcome, in primary_outcome.unit
field_notes.power.cv: stated coefficient of variation (percent); with baseline_mean it gives power.residual_sd
field_notes.power.residual_sd: in primary_outcome.unit when that is set; when an effect has a unit and no SD or CV is stated, residual_sd is absent, assumptions says "not stated: asked", and the scale question is asked
field_notes.analysis.posthoc: post-hoc comparisons the question asks for: {type: vs_control | pairwise | none, control: exact level label (vs_control), factor: the factor compared, adjust: emmeans method (absent = Bioana default: Holm; Dunnett for vs_control)}. Absent when not stated, and never for a two-level factor (its one comparison is the main test). A control word with no matching label names the first level of a counted factor with unnamed levels ("wild type", "genotype_2", ...), recorded in assumptions
field_notes.primary_outcome.event: survival: what counts as the event (germination, flowering, death, first lesion)
field_notes.primary_outcome.origin: survival: time zero (sowing, inoculation, infection, transplant)
field_notes.primary_outcome.censoring: survival: administrative at the end of follow-up (time stated when known); "; loss to follow-up" when losses are stated
field_notes.primary_outcome.event_column: survival: the event column ("event": 1 event, 0 censored, 2+ competing codes)
field_notes.primary_outcome.event_codes: survival: {"0": "censored", "1": event, "2": competing event} when something else can end observation (rot before germinating, death before flowering)
field_notes.analysis.survival: survival options, only what the question says: landmarks (times named), rmst_tau ("within the first N days"), logrank_weight (fh_1_0 early, fh_0_1 delayed), aft (how much longer/faster), life_table (scoring interval), strata (stated blocks when fewer than 10)
field_notes.power.events_required: survival: Schoenfeld events, 1:1, from target_hazard_ratio, alpha 0.05, power 0.8
field_notes.power.event_probability: survival: stated share of units with the event by the end of follow-up
field_notes.power.units_required: survival: events_required / event_probability / (1 - loss_fraction), when event_probability is stated
field_notes.primary_outcome.categories: class labels in the order named, reference first; nominal (3+ unordered classes) or binary (2); from "classified as A, B or C" or an expected ratio
field_notes.analysis.expected_ratio: {label: weight} from a stated ratio (3:1, 9:3:3:1, 1:2:1); labels are the categories in order, else class_1.. (asked); a one-group study (design single_group, model y ~ 1)
field_notes.analysis.correlation: {variables, method}: traits whose relationship is asked; variables[0] is primary_outcome.name (column primary_outcome), the rest are secondary_outcomes; method stated or pearson (assumption)
field_notes.secondary_outcomes: [{name, column}] traits measured besides the primary outcome; each has its own column in sample_metadata_template.tsv
field_notes.analysis.agreement: {rater_column: "rater", score_column: "primary_outcome", unit_column, scale: nominal | ordinal | continuous, levels}: raters or methods scoring the same units; rater is a within-unit factor (one template row per unit and rater)
field_notes.analysis.survival.cluster: survival with subsamples per unit (seeds per tray cell): the unit column is their cluster; the template has one row per subsample (column subsample)
field_notes.analysis.covariates: [{term: covariate|covariate2|..., name, column, unit, transform: log|log10|log2|sqrt, mean, sd}] (mean and sd only when stated): measured numeric predictors, one value per unit, blank columns in sample_metadata_template.tsv (not the layout)
field_notes.analysis.regression: {predict_at: [{name: value}], robust: "mm"} only when the question says so
field_notes.analysis.stat_tests: robust tests asked: "robust" (trimmed means) or a WRS2 id (yuen, yuen_paired, t1way, t2way, rmanova_trimmed, bwtrim)
field_notes.power.method: a-priori (pwr): pwr.t.test (2 groups), pwr.anova.test (k groups), pwr.r.test (correlation), pwr.2p.test (2 proportions, ES.h), pwr.chisq.test (expected ratio, w), pwr.f2.test (regression, u covariates, n_total = v + u + 1); none for logistic regression or survival (events)
field_notes.power.effect_size: with power.effect_size_name (d, f, r, h, w, f2): stated, or Cohen's medium value
field_notes.factors[].role: "adjustment" for a factor only adjusted for (additive, not part of the goal)
field_notes.analysis.adjust_for: names of adjustment factors ("adjusting for sex"); goal_terms leave them out
